# loopway

> loopway is a runner for bots. It hears events from the services you use, keeps each one as a CloudEvent in an inbox, routes them to bots by their rules, and runs each bot on your machines with the agent it's set to: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Hermes.

If a person asks you to set up loopway, make an inbox, or make a bot, the steps are below. Everything is done with the `loopway` CLI, which talks to {{base_url}}.

## Concepts

- **Org**: owns inboxes and bots. Every user has a personal org; shared orgs can have several members.
- **Inbox**: listens to one source, named by its `source_type`: `github`, `linear`, `vercel`, `granola`, `resend`, `schedule` (a message each hour, or each day at a UTC hour you pick) or `loopway` (messages posted straight to the inbox, so bots and backends can message each other). The source's webhook points at the inbox, which checks the signature and keeps the message; a `schedule` inbox takes no webhooks and fills itself. `loopway inbox create` prints the webhook URL and, for `github` and `loopway`, where loopway makes the secret, the secret, once; `loopway inbox show <inbox>` prints the URL and setup again, but not the secret. For `vercel`, `linear`, `granola` and `resend`, the sender makes the secret and you paste it in with `loopway inbox update <inbox> --secret ...`.
- **Message**: one stored delivery: the CloudEvent (its `type`, e.g. `com.github.issues.opened`, and `data`), when it arrived, and its place in arrival order. Nothing is marked done.
- **Bot**: reads the messages of one or more inboxes in arrival order and keeps a cursor, so it knows where it left off. A bot has a prompt, rules, a harness and a model. The harness is the coding agent its sessions run in: `claude` (Claude Code), `codex` (Codex), `cursor` (Cursor), `hermes` (Hermes) or `script` (a shell command, kept as the bot's prompt, for bots that act on an API's answer themselves), picked with `loopway bots create --harness <name>` and changed with `loopway bots update --harness <name>`. The model is one that agent takes. A new bot starts at the newest message, so it doesn't replay history.
- **Thread**: one session of the bot's agent working on a related set of messages. For GitHub, a thread is an issue and the PRs linked to it.
- **Level of automation**: loopway records one on every thread. Level 2: a person started it. Level 3: a bot started it and a person took part. Level 4: no person took part; bots start the work and finish it. (Level 1 is a person asking a model and doing the work themselves, so there is nothing for loopway to run.) Levels 3 and 4 are what loopway is for.
- **Runner**: a machine running `loopway bots run`. It belongs to one org and runs that org's bots.

## How a bot's rules work

Rules decide which thread each message goes to. A bot's rules are a list; the first rule whose `types` globs match the message's type applies (`*` matches any run of characters). Each rule has:

- `types`: list of event-type globs, e.g. `["com.github.*"]`.
- `subject`: a CEL expression over the message returning the thread key it belongs to (e.g. `owner/repo#12`), or `''` for none.
- `related`: optional CEL expression returning more thread keys the message also names (e.g. issues a PR body closes), so they join the same thread.
- `authorKind`: optional CEL expression returning `'human'` or `'bot'` for who made the message, or `''` when unknown. A thread's level of automation comes from it: `2` if the first message was from a person, `4` if from a bot, and a person's later message moves `4` to `3`.
- `action`: a CEL expression returning `'attach'` (deliver the message to the thread, creating it if needed) or `'skip'` (drop the message). Always set it, even to `'attach'`, so the rule says what it does (loopway treats a missing `action` as `'attach'`).

In expressions, `data` is the event payload and `event_type` its type; `action` can also read `subject`, `related` and `held` (whether a thread already holds one of those subjects). `regex_all(text, pattern[, flags])` returns every match of a JavaScript regex as a list of strings. A message with an empty subject and no related keys belongs to no thread.

The default `github-threads` preset routes every GitHub issue, PR, comment and review to a thread per issue or PR, attaches CI runs to their PR, and starts a session of the bot's agent per thread. Its prompt sets up worktrees with Claude Code's `EnterWorktree` tool, so edit that step for another agent. It is a good starting point: `loopway bots create --preset github-threads` copies its prompt and rules, and they can be edited afterwards on the bot's page.

## CLI

Install and log in:

```
curl -fsSL {{base_url}}/install.sh | sh   # needs Node 22+
loopway login              # emails a one-time code; new emails get an account
loopway whoami
```

Core commands:

```
loopway orgs                                  # your orgs
loopway orgs create <slug>                    # a shared org
loopway orgs use <slug>                       # the org commands work in without --org
loopway orgs add-member <slug> <email>

loopway inbox create --name <n> --source github --events issues,pull_request --secret <s> [--org <slug>]
loopway inbox list
loopway inbox show <inbox>                    # webhook URL, secret setup, message count
loopway inbox update <inbox> [--name n] [--events a,b] [--secret s]
loopway inbox update <inbox> --every hour|day [--hour <0-23, UTC>] --message <type>=<text>   # a schedule inbox's rhythm and messages

loopway messages list <inbox> [--type 'com.github.pull_request.*'] [--limit 20]
loopway messages get <inbox> <message> --data

loopway bots create --name <n> --preset github-threads --harness claude --model sonnet --inbox <inbox>[,<inbox>] [--org <slug>]
loopway bots list
loopway bots show <bot>
loopway bots update <bot> [--name n] [--harness h] [--model m] [--inbox a,b]
loopway bots messages <bot>                   # what the bot would read next
loopway bots threads <bot>                    # the bot's threads
loopway bots run [--max 3] [--interval 5]     # run all your bots; loopway.json can give each its own directory
```

`<inbox>` and `<bot>` are an id or an exact name, looked up in one org: `--org <slug>`, else the one `loopway orgs use` chose, else your only org. Lists work the same way. Commands say which org they used. Read commands take `--json`. Without a terminal, `inbox create` runs from flags alone, so pass every flag; `bots create` always needs `--name`, `--preset`, `--harness`, `--model` and `--inbox`. For `linear`, `vercel`, `granola` and `resend` inboxes the sender makes the secret: add the webhook in the sender, then give loopway the secret with `loopway inbox update <inbox> --secret <s>`.

## Typical setup

1. `loopway login`
2. `loopway inbox create` for the source, then add the webhook URL, and the secret `loopway inbox create` printed, in the sender (for GitHub, a repo or org webhook with JSON content type).
3. `loopway bots create --name <n> --preset github-threads --harness <harness> --model <model> --inbox <inbox>`
4. Run `loopway bots run`:
   - with one repo, run it in that repo;
   - with several repos, run it from a parent directory with a `loopway.json` that maps each bot to its repo: `{"bots": {"<bot name>": {"cwd": "path/relative/to/here"}}}`.
